rebuttal.challenge: WP19 already defines hidden-index fallback, so no missing behavior remains.
rebuttal.result: Partly succeeds: resolver and hidden predicate are already sufficiently specified. Fails for enumeration: §3.4 explicitly limits natural candidates to 0/1 while fixed R enumerates every nonempty natural position before hidden positions. Resolver cannot supply a missing menu candidate.

rebuttal.challenge: Three natural entries are invalid author input, or are truncated by compilation/registration.
rebuttal.result: Rejected by directly read schema, active list conversion, generic compilation, species validations/constructor and symbol registration. All three fixture identities are defined. No two-entry restriction occurs on this bounded chain; no compiler run claimed.

rebuttal.challenge: WP72 already lists the species table, therefore the candidate contract is covered.
rebuttal.result: Its index-write/cache-clear part is correct and retained. It neither overrides WP19 natural0/1 enumeration nor explains H labels based solely on index. A corrected shared WP19 contract plus a precise index-label consumer reference suffices; no separate debug root.

rebuttal.challenge: No hidden ability means PATCH must fail under the actual handler.
rebuttal.result: Rejected: after confirmation, handler selects the last enumerated pair whose index is 2, before the current-hidden/ZYGARDE guards. A third natural item can satisfy that lookup. The name used in the success notice and actual subsequently resolved ability can differ.

corrected_expected_behavior.candidate_rule: Enumerate every nonempty natural entry in its original position order with that zero-based position; then every nonempty hidden entry in its order with position+2. Do not collapse equal indices or assume a third natural candidate is a third naturally resolved slot.
corrected_expected_behavior.resolver_retained: Index≥2 reads the hidden entry; absent hidden entry falls back to the individual identifier low bit for natural lookup, then natural0 fallback. Stored index is retained; hidden predicate tests that index, not the identity of the resolved ability.
corrected_expected_behavior.minimal_vector: Artificial valid inert base-species data: natural [OVERGROW,CHLOROPHYLL,TORRENT], hidden empty. Enumeration returns (OVERGROW,0),(CHLOROPHYLL,1),(TORRENT,2). This is author configuration, not a claim about a bundled default species.
corrected_expected_behavior.patch_projection: Ordinary successful confirmation/refresh/messages, non-egg non-Hyper non-ZYGARDE individual initially index0, even identifier, one default PATCH: message names TORRENT, index becomes2, cache is cleared at assignment; resolver returns OVERGROW and hidden predicate is true. Handler returns true; ordinary consumable wrapper deducts one. Final cache emptiness is not promised if a later consumer has already resolved it.
normal_and_boundary_vectors: Only two natural entries and no hidden entries: PATCH has no index2 candidate and returns false, consuming none.
Three natural entries plus first hidden BLAZE: both (TORRENT,2) and (BLAZE,2) remain in that order; PATCH uses the latter name and resolves BLAZE.

Possible-ability debug lists every pair; every index≥2 gets H, selecting a pair writes its index and clears cache, not its displayed identity. CAPSULE still uses only index0/1 and refuses currently hidden-index individuals.
Confirmation cancel, already-hidden index, ZYGARDE, and invalid referenced identities retain their actual separate failure gates; a valid third entry does not bypass them.

accepted_claims: Enumeration is not capped at two natural entries.
Natural and hidden entries can share index2; ordering is retained.
PATCH eligibility/name and resolver result require distinct consumer semantics.
The independent implementation risk is lost author-list behavior and wrong consumption/identity, not only prose style.
excluded_claims: Default bundled Pokémon spontaneously gain a third naturally resolved ability.
A third candidate creates a third natural resolution slot.
WP19 hidden fallback or WP72 index writes are wholly absent.
Any arbitrary malformed PBS input compiles successfully.
Future implementation must reproduce an anomaly or a reference API.

required: Correct the shared enumeration rule without changing the already-correct resolver/predicate.
Cover artificial three-natural/empty-hidden, two-natural/empty-hidden and colliding hidden-index cases; expose PATCH message/index/actual identity/consumption separately.
Keep debug H labeling and index-only selection consistent with the corrected shared contract; cross-reference is sufficient and does not demand duplicate algorithms.
Retain normal item guards, successful dependency premises, author-config label and NOT_EXECUTED status.
optional: An additional fourth-or-later natural entry example is useful but not necessary once the unbounded rule and collision are explicit.
no_required_revision: Existing WP19 hidden fallback/predicate, WP03 generic identity/list rules and WP18 field defaults need no independent new defect.

history_relation.scope: No known prior closed control is reopened; no absence-of-history claim beyond searched current materials. Parent owns final history join.

unknowns: Actual custom PBS compilation and UI/media run not executed.
Plugin/dynamic overrides and broader author-data combinations not audited.
Future compatibility policy is outside this fact review.

confidence.basis: Independent producer, compiler/constructor and all three located enumeration callers read; opposite current rules considered.

rebuttal.result: Rejected after independently distinguishing calls. The first read at stored0 returns0 and does not submit. The explicit prompt submission then writes1. Refresh reads while timestamp is still absent, obtains0 different from stored1 and submits0. Outer continuation calls the handler with original requested1 but does not write form1 again.

rebuttal.challenge: Ordinary party UI does not read form during this refresh, or its final refresh restores1.
rebuttal.result: Rejected by Item→Use→item utility→bottle→party screen refresh→panel reset→icon reset→species icon dynamic form chain. After outer timestamp becomes fresh, hard refresh and refreshSingle read no-change from HOOPA handler and retain stored0.

rebuttal.result: Rejected by the table heading and its explicit responsibility for success state/inventory output. Correct the consumer result, rather than requiring an invented atomic/rollback policy.

rebuttal.result: AX19 covers learning rejection/abandonment after a form write, not refreshing before the time-setting handler. B16 relevant active fields, current vectors, finite B21 relevant leaves and originals do not supply the bottle result or retract WP66-A §8.

corrected_expected_behavior.summary: Legal non-egg FURFROU stored1, forced absent, timestamp integer t, nonbattle/nonstorage, first relevant dynamic read at t+432001, valid preceding scene/data/dependencies: opening summary reaches individual sprite lookup, commits stored0 and clears timestamp before resource matching. Cache clear, recomputation and conditional Pokédex registration follow. Recomputation is an operation, not proof every numeric value changes; later display may populate caches again.
corrected_expected_behavior.same_value_boundary: Dynamic reading commits only a nonempty result different from stored form. Explicit ordinary and prompt form submissions still execute their commit effects for equal values. Existing WP18/WP21 and FM04/FM40 already cover this distinction; no new mandatory same-value defect.
corrected_expected_behavior.bottle_premises: Normal default HOOPA stored0, timestamp absent, forced absent, alive/non-egg/non-Shadow/non-Hyper, no mail (ordinary Item menu available), normal party panel/icon already built and not disposed, nonbattle/nonstorage, default KeyItem bottle inventory1, all resources/messages/data/registration dependencies successful, no plugin/external mutation; prompt and final refresh finish within the three-day window.
bottle_order: The initial dynamic read returns0 equal to stored0; it performs no form submission or timestamp maintenance.
Prompt-type submission writes requested1 and clears ability cache, then begins the callback before its requested-form handler.

Callback refresh resets the same party member panel/icon. Dynamic form read still sees absent timestamp, returns0, and submits0; inner time handler clears the timestamp, then recomputes and conditionally registers.

Callback message completes. The outer handler receives original requested1 and records the current integer time. It does not rewrite form1. Outer recomputation/registration consume the actual stored0 through the species record; they do not certify form1 as seen.

The item handler returns true; ordinary party utility clears annotations, hard-refreshes, and returns true without consuming this KeyItem. The menu refreshes the selected member once more. Fresh timestamp makes further dynamic reads preserve0. Final observation: stored form0, fresh timestamp, bottle1.
normal_and_boundary_vectors: FURFROU at exactly t+432000 does not revert. Battle/storage flags suppress dynamic submission; forced0 returns0 while stored1/t remain. These guards suppress reading-triggered submission, not every explicit form write.
HOOPA stored0 with an already-fresh timestamp: ordinary bottle use retains1 and refreshes the timestamp. Absence of timestamp and presence of fresh timestamp are different inputs.
Direct ordinary submission to1 without a middle dynamic read produces1 with a fresh timestamp. This is a contrast entry, not a replacement for the normal party chain.
After the first bottle result0/fresh-time, another normal use within the window retains1; a subsequent1→0 use clears time. No claim that every use or every form item fails.

Resource failure after a dynamic form read does not imply rollback of an already completed submission; successful final UI/return requires normal dependencies. Real media and host results remain unverified.
